title: Privacy Policy
summary: This notice explains what Dayli handles, who can see shared content, the known providers, and how to make a privacy request.

blocks.text: This Privacy Policy is effective from 4 October 2026. It describes the current Dayli deployment and what the operator has not yet verified. Reading this notice or following a link does not record consent. When registration becomes available, Dayli records acknowledgement of this notice alongside explicit acceptance of the current Terms and a 16+ declaration. Acknowledgement is not broad consent to unrelated processing.

Dayli is operated by agroupforcoders, an informal group based in New Zealand, not a registered company. Contact agroupforcoders@gmail.com with privacy, access, correction, under-16, security, and deletion requests. The operator reviews messages at this address personally.

Dayli is intended for people worldwide aged 16 and over. Registration requires an explicit, initially unchecked 16+ declaration and acceptance of the effective Terms. Neither displaying the documents nor a previous sign-in establishes acceptance. Dayli does not ask for a birth date or identity document by default. Report a possible under-16 account by email for individual review and appeal, not automatic deletion.

To create and run an account, Dayli handles your username, public name if you provide one, email address, account identifier, password hash, account and session records, session IP address, user agent, verification and password-recovery records, and rate-limit records. Dayli does not store passwords as plaintext.

Dayli supports email and password accounts. Google sign-in may be available when it is enabled for the deployment. A Google identity is not linked to an existing Dayli account only because the email addresses match. Where configured, Resend sends password-recovery and verification emails.

Dayli handles the journal content and social information needed for its features. This includes posts, captions, ratings, optional weather condition, temperature and place name, tomorrow notes, audiences, release times, revisions, friendships, friend requests, blocks, direct messages, message edits, message reactions, and message-request decisions. Earlier post revisions can remain stored when a post is edited. Dayli does not store coordinates for the optional weather snapshot.

The mobile app stores a bearer session, cached identity, and unsent drafts in protected device storage. Selected media may be compressed and uploaded to Dayli's private object storage while a post is still being edited, before it is submitted or visible to anyone else. If push delivery is enabled and a recipient opts in, Dayli stores a protected device token and may send the sender's name and direct-message text through Firebase to that device. A notification can appear on a device lock screen, and content already delivered cannot be recalled.

Dayli uses account and session information to sign people in, protect accounts, recover passwords, apply rate limits, and operate available features. It uses posts, friendships, and blocks to decide who can view a post. It uses direct-message information to deliver and display messages to the people in a conversation. It uses device registration information to send notifications when that feature is enabled.
Dayli does not use personal content for research or to train AI systems. Content is server-readable, so this is not end-to-end encrypted messaging or journaling.

Solo and unreleased posts are for their author. A released friends-audience post from a public account can be read by anyone, including a visitor without an account. On a private account, active friends can read released friends-audience posts. Direct messages are available to conversation participants under the current access rules. Blocking limits future access for the affected signed-in accounts, but cannot take back information someone already saw, copied, or saved.

Dayli uses Neon PostgreSQL for application data and Cloudflare services for storage and application delivery. Depending on configuration, Google may process sign-in, Firebase may deliver mobile push, and Resend may process authentication email. If a person chooses weather by location in the mobile composer, their phone sends the approximate location to Open-Meteo and its own geocoder to obtain weather and a place name. If they search for a place, the search and weather request go to Open-Meteo. Only the resulting condition, temperature, and place name are sent to Dayli with the post. The operator has not verified the location of every copy, log, recovery operation, or provider process. We do not promise storage or processing in any one region.

The operator reports using Cloudflare-provided analytics. The enabled analytics products, identifiers, logs, purposes, and retention settings have not yet been inventoried. We do not claim that Dayli has no analytics or tracking.

Account content may be retained indefinitely while no verified account-deletion process is operating. Provider recovery copies, recovery history, object versions, and log-retention settings remain unverified. The planned 7-day cancellation, 14-day active cleanup, and 30-day backup expiry are not live service commitments. Dayli does not use a backup to selectively restore content you deleted, but we cannot promise that every provider recovery copy has expired.

Signed-in users can request one owner-scoped, versioned ZIP export from /account/export. When ready, its authenticated download remains available for 24 hours unless account access ends sooner. The archive contains approved owned records and excludes received message bodies and other people's private data; it is not a full response to every formal access request. Dayli does not yet provide verified account deletion or physical purge. Contact agroupforcoders@gmail.com about access, correction, or deletion. The operator will review requests under applicable law, but email does not trigger an automated deletion process, and removal is not currently verified as available.

Dayli uses access controls and secure session handling, but no system can guarantee absolute security. The operator approves policy changes and normally gives 30 days of notice for material Terms changes. An urgent shorter period requires an explained notice. Publishing this notice does not by itself open registration or verify a deletion process.
